title: Longing and Unreal Wishes in Testimony

sections.content:
You know *ojalá* and *quién* with the pluperfect subjunctive from B2 Unit 16, and *ojalá* with the imperfect subjunctive from B2 Unit 15. In testimony and chronicles of migration, speakers move back and forth between present longing and past regret using three high-register patterns.

1. **Present unreal wish vs past regret with *¡quién…!*:** *¡Quién pudiera!* (imperfect subjunctive) expresses an impossible or unlikely wish about now ('If only I could!'), whereas *¡Quién hubiera podido!* (pluperfect subjunctive) expresses regret about a past chance that is gone ('If only I had been able to!'). In both, *quién* always takes a third-person singular verb even though it refers to the speaker.
2. **Standalone *si al menos…*:** a *si* clause without a main clause voices quiet regret or longing—imperfect subjunctive for the present (*¡Si al menos vivieran más cerca!*), pluperfect subjunctive for the past (*¡Si al menos hubiéramos guardado aquellas cartas!*).
3. **No conditional after *ojalá*, *quién*, or *si al menos*:** all three require the subjunctive, never *habría* or *podría*.

sections.title: Present longing vs past regret in testimony
rows: ¡Quién pudiera caminar otra vez por aquel muelle!
Imperfect subjunctive: unreal wish about the present.
¡Quién hubiera conservado la libreta de recetas!
Pluperfect subjunctive: regret about the past.
¡Si al menos tuviéramos una fotografía de la panadería!
Standalone si al menos + imperfect subjunctive (present).
¡Si al menos hubiéramos grabado la voz de mi abuelo!
Standalone si al menos + pluperfect subjunctive (past).

items.spanish: Al mirar el muelle al atardecer, la narradora susurra: «¡Quién pudiera volver por un día a la tierra natal!».
items.english: Looking at the pier at dusk, the narrator whispers: 'If only I could return for a day to my native land!'

items.spanish: En la sobremesa del domingo, alguien comenta con añoranza: «¡Quién hubiera guardado las cartas del viaje!».
items.english: During the Sunday after-meal talk, someone remarks with longing: 'If only I had kept the letters from the journey!'

items.spanish: ¡Si al menos hubiéramos celebrado aquel reencuentro antes de que cerrara la panadería!
items.english: If only we had celebrated that reunion before the bakery closed!

items.spanish: Ojalá las nuevas generaciones conservaran el mismo cariño por las historias de la mesa familiar.
items.english: If only the new generations kept the same affection for the stories at the family table.

sections.content: Remember that *¡quién!* in a wish always governs the third-person singular verb (*¡Quién pudiera!*, *¡Quién hubiera sabido!*), even when the speaker means 'I'. Never conjugate it in the first person (*¡Quién hubiéramos!* is ungrammatical), and never use the conditional (*¡Quién podría!*).
